chunks: And it is narrated from Saʿd ibn al-Hasan, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
That he was asked about a man who swears that he will not sell his merchandise for such-and-such, then it later appears otherwise to him. He said: “He may sell, and he does not offer expiation.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man about whom the legal ruling is asked
key_terms.ثُمَّ يَبْدُو لَهُ: then he later changes his view or something occurs to him
key_terms.لَا يُكَفِّرُ: he is not required to offer expiation
key_terms.يَحْلِفُ: he swears or takes an oath

ai.seo_question: If someone swears not to sell his goods at a certain price and later changes his mind, must he pay expiation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about an oath concerning the sale of merchandise. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that if a person swears not to sell at a certain price and then changes his mind, he may proceed with the sale and no expiation is required.
